Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

IS:1282.1M8 

Indian Standard 

SPECIFICATION FOR 
BICYCLE COTTER PINS, WASHERS AND NUTS 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 14 October 1968, after the draft finalized by the 
Bicycles Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engi- 
neering Division Q^uncil. 

0.2 This standard was originally issued in 1958. The present revision 
has been taken up to express the various dimensions in metric units only 
rationalized to the extent practicable. Reference has also been made to 
bicycle threads as an interim measure till the changeover to metric system 
is effective. 

0,3 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on bicycles, their 
parts and accessories, prepared by the Institution at the iustance of the 
Tariff Commission and the Development Council for Bicycle industry, 

0.4 Bicycle cotter pins covered in this standard are intended for fitting on 
the cranks of two standard sizes ( 22 and 24 ) of bicycles, in use in the 
country. Washers of two types, namely, plain and spring, Ixave been covered 
in this specification. The purchaser should indicate in his enquiry and 
order, the type of washer required with the cotter pin wherever these are 
used. 

0*5 It may be pointed out that the requirements in regard to materials 
specified in this standard are only the minimum and the use of other 
materials having characteristics equivalent or superior to those specified 
in the standard is not precluded. 

0.6 In preparing this standard, assistance has been derived from Data 
Sheet No. 33a, Sheet No. 4 (Oct 1948) * Bottom bracket and crank 
assemblies, cotter, nut and washer' issued by the British Cycle and Motor 
Cycle Manufacturers and Traders Union Ltd. 

0.7 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this 
standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, express- 
ing the result of a test, sliail be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 
The number of significant places retained in the rounded oft' value should 
be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 



•Rulci for rounding off numrrical values ( nvistd ). 



I8il282-19«S 

1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard covers the requirements for bicycle cotter pins, their 
washers ( spring and plain ) and nuts for two standard sizes ( 22 and 24) of 
bicycles in use in the country. 

2. MATERIAL 

2*1 Cotter pins, plain washers and nuts shall be manufactured from steel 
conforming to 18:226-1962*. 

2.2 The spring washers shall be manufactured from spring steel having a 
minimum tensile strength of 70 kgf^'mm' and at least 1 5 percent elongation 
( gauge length 5*65 y/'\) when tested according to IS : 1521-19601. Suit- 
able steels for this purpose may be selected from IS : 1570-1961 J. 

3. DIMENSIONS 

3.1 The main dimensions for cottor pins shall be as given in Fig. 1 . 

3w2 The main dimensions for nuts shall be as given in Fig. 2 {see also 
IS:1364.1967§).

4. WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

4*1 The slope and cut of cotter pins shall be as given in Fig, 1 so as to 
facilitate accurate and tight fitting of the cranks on the centre axle. The 
threaded portion shall be accurate so as to facilitate tightening of the nuts 
to keep the cranks free from any shake or play. 

4.2 Cotter pins, washers and nuts shall be zinc plated to Service Condiiion 
No. 2 (Classification No. Fe Zn 12) of IS : 1573-I970* or cadmium 
plated to Service Condition No. 2 (Classification No, Cd8 ) of IS: 1572- 
I968t or nickel-chrome plated to Service Grade No. 1 ( Classification No. 
S NilOb Cr r ) of IS : 1068-1968^ 

5. PACKING 

5.1 Cotter pins, washers and nuts shall be wrapped in waterproof greased 
paper and then securely packed in strong cardboard boxes in accordance 
with the best prevalent trade practice. The boxes shall be labelled with 
the nnanufacturer's name or trade-mark, particulars of quantity and des- 
cription of contents, and name of country of origin. 

5.1A The cardboard boxes may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 

Note — The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, I9S6 and the Rules and Regulations made there- 
under. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys 
the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that 
standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control 
which IS devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the producer. Standard 
marked products are als.> continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that 
standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may 
be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 

6. SAMPLING 

5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the supplier and the purchaser, 
he procedure as given in IS: 2500 (Part I)-1963§ shall be followed for 
sampling inspection. The inspection level ar\d sampling plan as given 
in 6J,1 and 6.1.2 shall be followed. 

6.1.1 The scale of sampling shall be corresponding to inspection level IV 
given in Table I of IS : 2500 ( Part I)-1963§. 

6.1.2 The sampling plan to be followed shall be corresponding to 
Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) value of 2*5 percent given in Table II 
of IS : 2500 ( Part I)-1963§.
